div.div:
byId — the lookup
An update is a spread of one entry, so nothing else in the store changes identity. Object key order is not something to render from.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 366px; height: 1px; padding-top: 349px; margin-left: 430px;

div.div:
allIds — the order
The list renders by mapping this array, so order is explicit. A sorted or filtered view is a second id array, never a re-sorted byId.

div.div: Redux Toolkit's createEntityAdapter calls the two halves entities and ids — the identical shape, plus upsertOne / removeMany / getSelectors and a sortComparer.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe center; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 756px; height: 1px; padding-top: 615px; margin-left: 40px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: var(--dg-warn-fg);

display: inline-block; font-size: 12px; font-family: 'IBM Plex Sans',-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI',Roboto,sans-serif; color: var(--dg-warn-fg); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div: The dictionary answers "give me this one"; the array answers "in what order" — neither does the other job. And deleting an entity leaves its id behind in every array that referenced it, so decide on a cascade before you need one.
